plans.title: Build AlphaGo from Scratch

plans.prereq: You should be fluent with Python and NumPy arrays and know what a convolution, a softmax and gradient descent do; no prior knowledge of Go is needed.
plans.next: Next, work through the reinforcement learning problems on value functions and policy gradients to see how search-based training relates to model-free methods.

plans.title: Calculus for ML
plans.blurb: The calculus that training actually runs on, written as code: limits and continuity, derivatives and the chain rule, integrals over densities, Jacobians and Hessians, and the optimisation and autodiff machinery built from them.
plans.prereq: Comfortable Python and NumPy broadcasting, plus school-level derivatives; the matrix calculus section is easier if you have met eigenvalues and matrix products before.
plans.next: Move on to the optimisation-focused problems to see these gradients drive real update rules, or extend the autodiff problems into a small array-valued autograd engine.

plans.title: Cracking Computer Vision
plans.blurb: Build the vision stack from raw pixel arrays upward: image preprocessing, convolution and pooling, the box geometry behind object detectors, segmentation and detection losses, and the reshapes that turn images into transformer tokens. Every problem fixes its coordinate and rounding conventions, since that is where vision code usually breaks.
plans.prereq: Fluent NumPy indexing and broadcasting, and a working idea of what convolution and attention layers compute.
plans.next: Move on to how image and text encoders are trained jointly in multimodal models, or practise turning these primitives into end-to-end detection and segmentation system designs.

plans.title: Cracking Deep Learning
plans.blurb: Build the layers behind modern networks by hand in NumPy: activations, losses, initialisation, normalisation and backprop, then CNN, RNN and transformer blocks, and the pieces of autoencoders, VAEs and GANs. Every problem pins down shapes and conventions the way a framework does.
plans.prereq: Fluent Python and NumPy broadcasting, the chain rule, and matrix products; the Cracking ML and Calculus plans cover the groundwork.
plans.next: Go deeper into language or vision with the NLP and computer vision problems, or move on to diffusion and flow-matching models, which reuse the U-Net, attention and normalisation blocks practised here.

plans.title: Cracking ML Interviews
plans.blurb: Implement the classical machine learning toolkit from scratch: linear models, trees and ensembles, clustering, evaluation metrics and preprocessing. Each problem pins down its conventions exactly, the way an interviewer would.
plans.prereq: Comfortable Python and NumPy broadcasting, plus the basics of linear algebra, probability and gradients.
plans.next: Carry these building blocks into neural networks and training loops, or practise turning them into production pipelines in an ML system design setting.

plans.title: Cracking NLP
plans.blurb: Thirty-five NLP interview problems that start from raw strings and end at decoding, evaluation and tokenizer training. Each one pins down its conventions exactly, so you practise getting the details right rather than guessing them.
plans.prereq: Comfortable Python, dictionaries and NumPy indexing, plus the basic idea of a softmax and of training a model by gradient descent.
plans.next: Take these pieces into full Transformer language models and retrieval pipelines, where tokenizers, sampling and ranking meet real model weights.

plans.title: Cracking RL
plans.blurb: Thirty reinforcement learning interview problems, from Bellman equations and tabular TD control to bandits, DQN tricks, policy gradients, PPO and the preference losses behind RLHF. Environments are small arrays and every random draw is passed in, so each answer is exact.
plans.prereq: Comfortable NumPy indexing and broadcasting, plus expected values, conditional probability and the softmax function.
plans.next: Scale these pieces up with neural function approximation in PyTorch, or study how the RLHF losses here fit into a full language model post-training pipeline.

plans.title: CUDA Kernels
plans.blurb: Write GPU kernels from scratch with Numba CUDA: map threads to data, keep memory accesses coalesced, reduce across a block with shared memory and barriers, and finish with tiled convolutions and matrix multiplication.
plans.prereq: You should be comfortable with Python loops and NumPy arrays; no previous GPU experience is assumed, since the first section starts from a single element-wise kernel.
plans.next: Carry these ideas up a level with Triton and into model serving in Inference Engineering, where the same reductions and tiles show up as softmax, normalisation and attention kernels.

plans.title: Build a Diffusion Model from Scratch
plans.blurb: Write every piece of a denoising diffusion model in NumPy: the noise schedule, the forward process, a small time-conditioned denoiser, the training loss, and the DDPM, DDIM and ODE samplers. The last sections connect it to score matching and flow matching and finish with a complete train-and-sample loop.
plans.prereq: Comfort with NumPy broadcasting and the basic properties of the normal distribution (sums, scaling, mean and variance) is enough to start.
plans.next: Scale the toy pieces into a real PyTorch model trained on images, then explore latent diffusion, distillation for few-step sampling, and text conditioning with cross-attention.

plans.title: Inference Engineering Drills
plans.blurb: Build the pieces of an LLM serving engine in code: attention variants that shrink the KV cache, tiled attention, sampling and MoE routing, a paged and prefix-shared cache, speculative decoding, low-bit weight formats, and the schedulers, metrics and capacity models that decide what a deployment costs.
plans.prereq: Comfortable with PyTorch tensor code and with how causal attention in a Transformer works; knowing what a KV cache stores is a good starting point.
plans.next: Write the GPU kernels behind these components with the Triton plan, or follow a full model from training to serving in the LLM from-scratch plan.

plans.title: JAX for ML Systems
plans.blurb: Learn JAX the way ML systems engineers use it: pure functions transformed by grad, jit, vmap and scan, then the optimizers, numerics, decoding loops and collectives that real training and serving code is built from.
plans.prereq: Be comfortable with NumPy arrays and broadcasting and with how gradient descent trains a model; knowing attention helps from the inference sections on.
plans.next: Take these patterns to production serving in the Inference Engineering study plan, or drop one level down and write the kernels yourself in the Triton study plan.

plans.title: Linear Algebra for ML
plans.blurb: Build the linear algebra behind ML by hand: vectors and norms, matrix products, solving systems, the major factorisations (LU, QR, Cholesky, SVD, eigen), and then the ML methods that rest on them.
plans.prereq: You should be comfortable writing Python functions and slicing and broadcasting NumPy arrays.
plans.next: Move on to calculus for ML, where these matrix tools turn into gradients and Jacobians, or revisit the ML Maths lessons linked from each problem for the geometric picture.

plans.title: Language Modeling from Scratch
plans.blurb: Build a modern language model end to end, one exercise at a time: tokenizers and Transformer blocks, GPU kernels and parallelism, scaling laws, inference, evaluation, data pipelines and post-training with preferences and verifiable rewards. Each problem isolates one piece you would otherwise only see buried inside a large training codebase.
plans.prereq: You should be comfortable with Python, NumPy and PyTorch and know how attention and a Transformer block work; the PyTorch and Triton study plans are good preparation for the kernel sections.
plans.next: Continue with the Inference Engineering study plan for serving in more depth, or the reinforcement learning problems for the policy-gradient ideas behind RLHF and GRPO.

plans.title: Build Micrograd from Scratch
plans.blurb: Grow a tiny scalar autograd engine one piece at a time: measure slopes numerically, wrap numbers in Value nodes that remember their history, write backward rules and a topological backward pass, then stack neurons into an MLP and train it with your own gradients.
plans.prereq: Comfortable Python (classes, closures, operator overloading) and derivatives at school level; the chain rule is used constantly, so a quick refresher on it helps.
plans.next: Move from scalars to arrays: rewrite the engine on NumPy tensors with matrix-valued backward rules, or compare it with how PyTorch's autograd records and replays the same graph.

plans.title: NumPy Sheet
plans.blurb: Twenty-five short exercises that take you from building arrays to writing loop-free data transforms. Each problem uses one core NumPy idea on a small, realistic task: padding token batches, cutting image patches, forward-filling sensor gaps, finding the lag between two signals.
plans.prereq: You should be comfortable writing Python functions with lists and loops; no NumPy experience is assumed.
plans.next: Next, try the Linear Algebra plan, where these array skills become matrix factorisations, then build full models from scratch in Cracking ML.

plans.title: Optimization
plans.blurb: Build the optimizers behind model training from first principles: solve quadratics in closed form, read curvature from the Hessian, then implement gradient descent, momentum, AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam and L-BFGS, and race them against each other.
plans.prereq: Comfortable with NumPy arrays and matrix products, and with taking partial derivatives of simple functions.
plans.next: Apply these optimizers inside real networks in the deep learning plans, and study how learning-rate schedules and batch size interact at scale.

plans.title: Pandas Sheet
plans.blurb: Twenty-five hands-on exercises that cover the everyday pandas toolkit on realistic tables: messy exports, event logs, sensor feeds, sales ledgers and training metrics. You go from building and inspecting a DataFrame to cleaning it, summarising it by group and reshaping it between long and wide.
plans.prereq: You should be able to write Python functions using lists, dicts and loops; no previous pandas experience is needed.
plans.next: Continue with the NumPy plan to see the array machinery under every DataFrame, or the SQL plan to express the same joins, groupings and windows in a database, then put the skills to work in Cracking ML.

plans.title: Probability & Statistics
plans.blurb: Thirty problems that build statistics from the ground up in NumPy, from summary statistics and counting through distributions, sampling and the CLT, to hypothesis tests whose p-values you compute yourself without SciPy.
plans.prereq: Comfortable Python and NumPy arrays, plus school algebra; no statistics course assumed.
plans.next: Apply these tools to models that are built on them, such as Naive Bayes, Gaussian mixtures and A/B experiment pipelines, or revisit the ML Maths probability and inference lessons for the theory behind each test.

plans.title: PyTorch Sheet
plans.blurb: Thirty problems that build PyTorch fluency from tensors and autograd up to optimizers, data pipelines and the layers inside real models. Each one asks you to reproduce what a built-in does, from the raw weights, and match it exactly.
plans.prereq: You should know Python and basic NumPy array work, and roughly what a layer and a loss function are; the NumPy plan covers the array skills.
plans.next: Go deeper into architectures with Cracking Deep Learning, or follow attention into large language models in the Inference Engineering course.

plans.title: SQL Sheet
plans.blurb: Twenty-five SQLite queries on the tables an ML engineer actually meets: experiment logs, eval results, inference requests, clickstreams and model registries. You start with single-table SELECTs and work up to window functions, recursive CTEs and sessionizing events, with every problem pinning down the NULL, tie and boundary cases that trip people up.
plans.prereq: No SQL background is needed; it helps to know what a table, a row and a column are.
plans.next: Take the same analyses into Python with the Pandas plan, then use them on model outputs in the Metrics & Evaluation problems.

plans.title: Triton Kernels
plans.blurb: Thirty GPU kernel exercises, most of them written block by block in Triton, from a masked elementwise add to FlashAttention, split-K and block-pointer matmuls. Triton kernels are graded on a real GPU in Colab against a PyTorch reference of the same spec, and each explanation covers memory traffic, masking and the bugs that bite in practice.
plans.prereq: You should be at home with PyTorch tensors, shapes and strides; CUDA experience helps but is not required.
plans.next: Take the attention, KV-cache and normalisation kernels into serving with the Inference Engineering course, or compare them with their thread-level versions in the CUDA plan.

builds.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
builds.blurb: Combined momentum with per-parameter step sizes from a running average of squared gradients, plus a bias correction, giving the default optimiser for most of deep learning.
builds.intro: Adam tracks exponential averages of the gradient and of its square, corrects both for their zero initialisation, and steps each parameter by the ratio of the two. The paper also introduces AdaMax, which uses an infinity norm in place of the second moment. The steps build momentum, RMSProp, the Adam update, the full optimiser and decoupled weight decay, then compare them; the capstone runs Adam, Adam without bias correction and AdaMax on a noisy ill-conditioned quadratic.

steps.name: AdamW: decoupled weight decay
steps.note: The later fix that modern LLM training uses.

lesson_links.t: Adaptive methods: AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam, AdamW

builds.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
builds.blurb: The GPU-trained CNN that won ImageNet 2012 by a wide margin and started the deep learning era in computer vision.
builds.intro: AlexNet combined ReLU activations, local response normalisation, overlapping max pooling, dropout and aggressive data augmentation in a five-convolution, three-FC network. The steps build each ingredient, including the PCA colour augmentation; the capstone runs a miniature AlexNet with the paper's ten-crop test-time averaging.

steps.name: Overlapping max pooling
steps.note: Use window 3 and stride 2.

builds.title: Attention Is All You Need
builds.blurb: Replaced recurrence in machine translation with stacks of self-attention and feed-forward layers, so a whole sentence is processed in parallel.
builds.intro: The paper's encoder-decoder is built from four ideas: token embeddings plus a fixed sinusoidal position signal, scaled dot-product attention split into several heads, a position-wise feed-forward network, and residual connections wrapped in LayerNorm. The steps build each piece and then the two block types; the capstone stacks them into a full translation model whose output is next-token logits. Decoding with a beam closes the loop.

steps.name: Build a vocabulary
steps.note: Map tokens to ids, with special tokens for padding and sentence start.

steps.name: Scaled dot-product attention
steps.note: The $QK^\top/\sqrt{d_k}$ core, with a mask.

steps.name: Encoder block
steps.note: Self-attention and FFN sublayers, pre-LN and post-LN.

steps.name: Decoder block
steps.note: Adds causal masking and cross-attention to the encoder output.

steps.name: Beam search
steps.note: How the paper decodes translations, with a length penalty.

builds.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
builds.blurb: Introduced attention to neural translation: the decoder computes a fresh weighted average of all encoder states at every output step.
builds.intro: A bidirectional RNN encoder produces one annotation per source word. At each output step a small network scores every annotation against the previous decoder state, the softmax of the scores weights the annotations into a context vector, and the decoder consumes it together with the previous word. The steps build the GRU, the encoder-decoder and additive attention; the capstone wires the full teacher-forced model and returns the alignment matrix.

steps.name: Encoder-decoder without attention
steps.note: The fixed-vector bottleneck attention removes.

builds.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
builds.blurb: Normalised each layer's pre-activations over the mini-batch, which allowed much higher learning rates and made deep networks far less sensitive to initialisation.
builds.intro: BatchNorm standardises every unit with the batch mean and variance, then applies a learned scale and shift. Because each example's output depends on the whole batch, the backward pass must differentiate through the batch statistics, and at test time the layer switches to running averages. The steps build per-channel statistics, the layer itself, its per-example cousin LayerNorm, manual backprop and initialisation; the capstone trains a small classifier for one step and evaluates it in inference mode.

steps.name: BatchNorm in train and eval mode
LayerNorm for comparison
steps.note: Normalises over features instead of the batch, so it has no train/eval difference.

steps.name: Weight initialisation
steps.note: What BatchNorm makes much less critical.

builds.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
builds.blurb: Pre-trains a bidirectional Transformer encoder by predicting masked tokens and sentence order, then fine-tunes the same network for each downstream task.
builds.intro: BERT is an encoder-only Transformer. Its novelty is the pre-training setup: WordPiece inputs packed as `[CLS] A [SEP] B [SEP]` with segment embeddings, a masked-language-model objective that lets every position use both left and right context, and a next-sentence classifier on `[CLS]`. The steps build the input pipeline and the corruption scheme, then the encoder and two fine-tuning heads; the capstone computes both pre-training losses from one forward pass.

steps.name: WordPiece tokenization
steps.note: Greedy longest-match encoding with `##` continuation pieces.

steps.name: Fine-tuning: span extraction
steps.note: SQuAD-style start and end logits.

steps.name: Fine-tuning: token classification
steps.note: Align word labels to WordPiece tokens.

builds.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
builds.blurb: Found that model size and training tokens should scale roughly equally with compute, about 20 tokens per parameter, and showed a smaller model trained on more data beats a larger undertrained one.
builds.intro: The paper trains hundreds of models across sizes and token counts and estimates the compute-optimal split three ways: from the lower envelope of training curves, from IsoFLOP profiles, and from a parametric fit $L = E + A/N^\alpha + B/D^\beta$. The steps build FLOP counting, compute budgets, power-law fits with and without a loss floor, the IsoFLOP exponent and allocation rules; the capstone fits the parametric loss and derives the optimal model and data size for several budgets.

steps.name: Power law with a loss floor
Exponent from an IsoFLOP sweep
steps.note: The paper's second approach.

steps.name: Compute-optimal size from a fitted loss

builds.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
builds.blurb: Trained image and text encoders on 400 million image-caption pairs with a contrastive loss, producing a joint embedding space that classifies images zero-shot from class names.
builds.intro: CLIP embeds a batch of images and their captions, normalises both, and trains so that each image's most similar caption in the batch is its own, and vice versa. The result is a pair of encoders whose cosine similarity measures image-text agreement. The steps build the ViT input embedding, masked pooling for text features, the symmetric contrastive loss and its sigmoid alternative, and retrieval; the capstone turns class names and prompt templates into a zero-shot classifier.

steps.name: ViT patch embedding
steps.note: CLIP's best image encoders are ViTs.

steps.name: SigLIP's pairwise sigmoid loss
steps.note: A later replacement that drops the batch-wide softmax.

builds.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
builds.blurb: Showed that a model trained to predict the noise added to an image, then run as a long reverse chain, produces samples competitive with GANs.
builds.intro: The forward process adds Gaussian noise over $T$ steps on a fixed schedule, and has a closed form for jumping from $x_0$ straight to any $x_t$. A network learns to predict the added noise with a plain mean-squared error, and sampling runs the reverse chain from pure noise, removing predicted noise and adding a little fresh noise at each step. The steps build the schedule, the forward jump, the posterior, the loss, the timestep embedding and both algorithms; the capstone trains a toy model and samples from it.

steps.name: Timestep embedding
steps.note: How a real denoiser is told which step it is on.

lesson_links.t: Diffusion: the denoiser and its objective
Diffusion: sampling with DDPM and DDIM

builds.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
builds.blurb: A 671B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 37B active parameters per token, built on latent attention, fine-grained experts, bias-based load balancing and multi-token prediction.
builds.intro: Each DeepSeek-V3 layer pairs multi-head latent attention (MLA), which caches a small latent per token instead of full keys and values, with a DeepSeekMoE feed-forward: one shared expert plus many small routed experts chosen by sigmoid affinities. Load is balanced by adjusting per-expert routing biases instead of an auxiliary loss, and extra modules predict tokens further ahead during training. The steps build MLA, the router and the MoE machinery separately; the capstone assembles one full block.

steps.name: Multi-head latent attention
steps.note: Compressed KV plus a decoupled rotary key.

steps.name: KV-cache size: MHA, GQA and MLA
Top-k routing with balance statistics
steps.note: The auxiliary-loss approach V3 moved away from, for comparison.

steps.name: Block-wise FP8 quantization
steps.note: V3 trained in FP8 with fine-grained scaling.

lesson_links.t: How MoE Inference Differs From Dense Models

builds.title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
builds.blurb: Connects every layer in a block to all earlier layers by concatenation, so features are reused and each layer can be very narrow.
builds.intro: A dense block keeps a growing stack of feature maps: each layer reads the whole stack and appends $k$ new channels. Bottleneck 1×1 convolutions keep the 3×3 layers cheap, and transition layers compress channels and halve the resolution between blocks. The steps cover the convolution, normalisation and pooling pieces; the capstone builds a DenseNet-BC from blocks and transitions.

steps.name: 1×1 bottlenecks and their savings
steps.note: Counting how cheap convolutions reduce cost, the motivation for the BC variant.

builds.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
builds.blurb: Replaced the diffusion U-Net with a plain transformer over latent patches and showed sample quality improves steadily with compute.
builds.intro: DiT patchifies a latent like a ViT, runs transformer blocks over the tokens and unpatchifies the output into a noise prediction and a variance. The timestep and class label condition every block through adaptive LayerNorm: they regress a shift, a scale and a residual gate per sublayer, initialised so each block starts as the identity. The steps build patchification, the timestep embedding, one adaLN-Zero block and classifier-free guidance; the capstone is the full forward pass from latent to output.

steps.name: Classifier-free guidance
steps.note: DiT's best results use guidance with a null class label.

builds.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
builds.blurb: Showed that the KL-regularised RLHF objective can be optimised directly from preference pairs with a classification loss, with no reward model and no RL loop.
builds.intro: The optimal policy for a KL-penalised reward has a closed form, so the reward can be written in terms of the policy's log-probability ratio to a reference model. Substituting that into the Bradley-Terry preference likelihood cancels the intractable normaliser and leaves a loss on the policy alone. The steps build preference data, the Bradley-Terry loss, the DPO loss from token log-probabilities and the choice of length normalisation; the capstone computes sequence log-probabilities for a bigram model and takes one DPO gradient step.

steps.name: Bradley-Terry loss
steps.note: The preference model DPO inherits.

builds.title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning
builds.blurb: Learned to play dozens of Atari games from pixels with a single Q-learning agent, stabilised by experience replay and a periodically updated target network.
builds.intro: DQN is Q-learning with a convolutional network as the Q-function. Two additions make the combination stable: transitions are stored in a replay buffer and sampled at random, and the bootstrapped targets come from a frozen copy of the network that is refreshed only occasionally. The steps build tabular Q-learning, $\epsilon$-greedy exploration, the replay buffer, the target-network loss and the later Double, Dueling and prioritised-replay improvements; the capstone runs the whole training loop on a chain environment.

steps.name: Huber loss against a target network
Double DQN targets
steps.note: Later work that reduces overestimation.

builds.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
builds.blurb: Regularised neural networks by randomly zeroing units during training, approximately averaging an exponential number of thinned networks at test time.
builds.intro: During training each unit is kept with some probability and dropped otherwise, a different mask for every example and step. At test time the full network is used with activations scaled to match their training-time expectation; the inverted form does the scaling during training instead. The steps build the forward pass, inverted dropout and its channel-wise variant for feature maps; the capstone trains a regressor with explicit masks and compares deterministic prediction with Monte Carlo dropout.

steps.name: Channel dropout for feature maps
steps.note: Drops whole channels, since neighbouring pixels are strongly correlated.

builds.title: Finding Structure in Time
builds.blurb: Introduced the simple recurrent network, whose hidden state feeds back as context so the network can discover structure in sequences.
builds.intro: An Elman network copies its hidden layer into a context layer that is fed back at the next step, giving the recurrence $h_t = \tanh(x_tW_{xh} + h_{t-1}W_{hh} + b)$. Training it means backpropagating through the unrolled sequence, and the gradients through many steps tend to vanish or explode. The steps build the cell, a language model and training with truncated BPTT and clipping; the capstone computes full BPTT gradients and shows the vanishing effect.

steps.name: Score a batch with an RNN language model

builds.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
builds.blurb: Replaced hand-crafted region proposals with a small network on shared convolutional features, making two-stage detection fast and fully learned.
builds.intro: A region proposal network slides over the backbone's feature map, scoring and refining a set of anchor boxes at every position. Its top proposals, after NMS, are cropped from the same features and passed to a second head that classifies and refines them. The steps build anchors, IoU and box encodings, RPN training targets, NMS, RoIAlign and the feature pyramid that later versions add; the capstone turns raw RPN outputs into proposals.

steps.name: Anchor boxes over a feature map
RoIAlign
steps.note: From Mask R-CNN; it replaced the paper's RoI pooling.

steps.name: Feature pyramid fusion
steps.note: FPN, the standard multi-scale backbone for Faster R-CNN since 2017.

builds.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
builds.blurb: Made exact attention much faster and linear in memory by tiling it so the attention matrix never leaves on-chip memory, recomputing it in the backward pass.
builds.intro: Attention is bound by memory traffic, not arithmetic: writing and re-reading the $N\times N$ score and probability matrices dominates. FlashAttention processes query and key tiles in fast SRAM, combining partial softmaxes with an online rescaling, and stores only the output and one logsumexp per row. The backward pass rebuilds each probability tile from that logsumexp. The steps build reference attention, the online softmax and tiled forward passes in numpy, torch and Triton; the capstone adds the tiled backward pass.

steps.name: Forward kernel in Triton
steps.note: The same algorithm as a GPU kernel.

builds.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
builds.blurb: Trained continuous normalising flows without simulation by regressing a velocity field onto per-sample target velocities along simple paths from noise to data.
builds.intro: Pick a path from each noise sample to a data sample, such as a straight line, and its velocity is known in closed form. Regressing a network onto those conditional velocities learns a field whose ODE moves the whole noise distribution onto the data. Sampling integrates that ODE with a standard solver. The steps build the flow-matching loss, conversions between prediction targets and an ODE sampler; the capstone trains a small velocity model and integrates it with Euler or midpoint steps.

steps.name: Converting between noise, data and velocity targets
steps.note: Links flow matching to diffusion's $\epsilon$- and $v$-prediction.

steps.name: Euler ODE sampling
steps.note: The same integrator, written for a diffusion ODE.

builds.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
builds.blurb: Trained a generator by pitting it against a discriminator that learns to tell real samples from generated ones, with no likelihood and no Markov chains.
builds.intro: The discriminator is a binary classifier trained with cross-entropy on real and generated samples; the generator is trained to make the discriminator wrong. The two alternate, usually with a few discriminator steps per generator step, and the paper's practical trick is the non-saturating generator loss. The steps build the networks, the classifier loss and a single adversarial update; the capstone runs the full alternating loop on 1-D data and also asks how to evaluate the result.

steps.name: MLP forward pass
steps.note: Both players in the paper are MLPs.

steps.name: Evaluating samples with FID
steps.note: A later metric, now the standard way to compare GANs.

builds.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
builds.blurb: Combines Mamba-2's decay gate with DeltaNet's error-correcting state update, giving a linear-time recurrent layer that both forgets and overwrites precisely.
builds.intro: Linear attention keeps a matrix state that only accumulates. The delta rule turns it into a key-value memory that corrects the value stored under each key; a scalar decay gate lets the memory forget quickly. The steps go from linear attention through the gated recurrence to the chunkwise (WY/UT) form used for training; the capstone wraps the recurrence in the full layer with projections, short convolutions and a gated output norm.

steps.name: Mamba-2 scalar-gated scan
steps.note: Where the decay gate comes from.

steps.name: Gated delta rule, token by token
Chunkwise form with the WY/UT transform

builds.title: Gemma 3 Technical Report
builds.blurb: Extends the Gemma decoder to 128k-token contexts by making most layers sliding-window attention, with a global layer every few layers.
builds.intro: Gemma 3's block is a GQA decoder block with RMSNorm on both sides of each sublayer and QK-norm inside attention. The architecture change that matters most is the layer schedule: five local sliding-window layers for every global layer, with a small RoPE base for local layers and a large one for global layers. The steps cover sliding-window GQA, RoPE, the norm choices and the gated MLP; the capstone builds the interleaved stack.

steps.name: Causal GQA with a sliding window
Soft-capping vs QK-norm
steps.note: Gemma 2 capped logits; Gemma 3 normalises queries and keys instead.

steps.name: KV-cache size of local vs global layers

builds.title: GLM-4.5: Agentic, Reasoning, and Coding (ARC) Foundation Models
builds.blurb: A deep, narrow mixture-of-experts decoder with dense prefix layers, partial RoPE, QK-norm and a multi-token-prediction layer, trained for agentic and reasoning tasks.
builds.intro: GLM-4.5's architecture combines familiar parts in a particular way: GQA attention with QK-norm and rotary embeddings on only part of each head, a few dense layers at the bottom, MoE layers with a shared expert and sigmoid routing balanced by biases, and an MTP layer used for speculative decoding. The steps cover each part; the capstone builds a stack of dense and MoE layers.

builds.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
builds.blurb: Trained a 1.5B-parameter decoder-only Transformer on a large web corpus and showed it could perform many tasks zero-shot from a prompt.
builds.intro: GPT-2 is the template for modern decoder-only models: byte-level BPE, learned token and position embeddings, pre-LN blocks with causal multi-head attention and a GELU MLP, a final LayerNorm, and an output layer tied to the token embeddings. The steps go from the tokenizer to sampling; the capstone runs the forward pass and generates text greedily, including the context-window crop.

lesson_links.t: Trace the shapes through a transformer

builds.title: gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card
builds.blurb: OpenAI's open-weight MoE reasoning models: alternating banded and dense attention with learned sinks, YaRN-extended RoPE, and MXFP4 expert weights.
builds.intro: gpt-oss is a pre-norm MoE decoder. Attention layers alternate between a 128-token band and full causal attention, use grouped-query attention, and give every head a learned sink logit. RoPE is extended to 131k tokens with YaRN. Each MoE layer routes tokens to the top 4 experts, whose SwiGLU activations are clamped, and the expert weights are stored in MXFP4. The steps build each of these components; the capstone wires one full block.

builds.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
builds.blurb: Introduced Group Relative Policy Optimization, which replaces PPO's value network with rewards normalised across a group of sampled answers, the RL algorithm behind later open reasoning models.
builds.intro: For each question GRPO samples a group of answers, scores them, and uses each answer's reward relative to the group as its advantage, so no critic is trained. The loss keeps PPO's clipped ratio and adds a KL penalty to a reference model directly. The paper also compares outcome supervision, one reward per answer, with process supervision, a reward per reasoning step. The steps build group-relative advantages and their normalisation choices, KL estimators, the leave-one-out baseline and token aggregation; the capstone computes process-supervised advantages and the full loss.

steps.name: REINFORCE leave-one-out
steps.note: A closely related critic-free baseline.

lesson_links.t: PPO, LLM Reasoning, Importance Ratio, Advantage

builds.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
builds.blurb: Proposed the RNN encoder-decoder and the gated recurrent unit, a simpler two-gate alternative to the LSTM.
builds.intro: The GRU merges the LSTM's cell and hidden state and uses two gates: an update gate that interpolates between the old state and a candidate, and a reset gate that controls how much of the old state the candidate sees. The same paper introduced the encoder-decoder used for translation. The steps build the cell, the encoder-decoder and masked pooling; the capstone is a bidirectional GRU classifier that handles padding correctly.

builds.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
builds.blurb: Aligned GPT-3 with user intent through supervised fine-tuning, a reward model trained on human rankings, and PPO against that reward with a KL penalty.
builds.intro: The recipe has three stages. Supervised fine-tuning on demonstrations gives a starting policy; a reward model learns from human comparisons of sampled responses; and reinforcement learning maximises the learned reward while a KL penalty keeps the policy near the SFT model and a pretraining term limits regressions. The steps build the SFT loss mask, preference-data cleaning, the Bradley-Terry reward loss, KL-regularised rewards and an RLHF PPO step; the capstone runs the reward-model and RL stages end to end on a toy problem with exact expectations.

steps.name: PPO step with a reference-policy KL

builds.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
builds.blurb: Moved diffusion into the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder and conditioned it through cross-attention, the recipe behind Stable Diffusion.
builds.intro: A perceptual autoencoder compresses images to a small latent grid once, and the diffusion model only ever sees latents, which cuts training and sampling cost sharply. Text or other conditions enter the denoiser through cross-attention, with latent positions as queries and condition tokens as keys and values. The steps build the autoencoders, attention over latent positions, cross-attention in a decoder block, classifier-free guidance and the DDIM update; the capstone wires them into a guided sampler that decodes its final latent.

steps.name: VAE-regularised latents
steps.note: The paper's KL-regularised autoencoder keeps latents close to a standard normal.

steps.name: Cross-attention inside a block
steps.note: The same query-from-one-sequence, keys-from-another pattern conditions the denoiser on text.

lesson_links.t: Diffusion: sampling with DDPM and DDIM

builds.title: Large Language Diffusion Models
builds.blurb: Trains an 8B masked diffusion language model from scratch and shows it competes with autoregressive models of similar size, including on in-context learning and instruction following.
builds.intro: LLaDA replaces next-token prediction with masked diffusion: a bidirectional Transformer predicts all masked tokens of a sequence corrupted at a random rate $t$, with a $1/t$-weighted loss. Sampling starts from an all-mask answer and unmasks it over several steps. The steps build the corruption and loss, guidance and the bidirectional mask predictor; the capstone is the semi-autoregressive sampler with low-confidence remasking.

builds.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
builds.blurb: Showed that smaller decoder-only models trained on more tokens can match much larger ones, using a block design (RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU) that most open models now share.
builds.intro: The LLaMA block is a pre-norm decoder block with three substitutions: RMSNorm for LayerNorm, rotary position embeddings applied to queries and keys, and a SwiGLU feed-forward network. LLaMA 2 added grouped-query attention for its larger models. Each step builds one of these parts in isolation; the capstone stacks them into a full forward pass, and the last step shows how the model is decoded with a KV cache.

steps.name: Rotary position embeddings
steps.note: Both the interleaved and the rotate-half layouts.

steps.name: SwiGLU feed-forward
steps.note: Why the hidden width is about $\tfrac{8}{3}D$.

builds.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
builds.blurb: Fine-tuned large models by freezing the pretrained weights and training a low-rank update, cutting trainable parameters by orders of magnitude with no added inference latency.
builds.intro: A frozen weight $W_0$ gets a trainable update $\frac{\alpha}{r}AB$ with $A$ random and $B$ zero, so training starts exactly at the pretrained model. Only the thin factors receive gradients and optimiser state, and after training the update can be merged into $W_0$. The steps build a linear layer, low-rank approximation and the SVD that underlies it; the capstone fine-tunes adapters on a frozen layer and merges them.

steps.name: Best low-rank approximation
steps.note: What a rank-$r$ update can and cannot represent.

builds.title: Long Short-Term Memory
builds.blurb: Adds a gated, additively updated memory cell to recurrent networks so error signals can flow across long time lags.
builds.intro: The LSTM keeps a cell state that is updated additively and protected by multiplicative gates: input and output gates in the original paper, and the forget gate added by Gers et al. in 2000, which every modern LSTM includes. The steps build the gates, a single cell forward and backward, and a bidirectional LSTM; the capstone evaluates an LSTM language model over a padded batch.

steps.name: Bidirectional LSTM over a padded batch

builds.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
builds.blurb: Made state-space models input-dependent so they can select what to remember, matching transformers on language modelling with linear-time training and constant-memory decoding.
builds.intro: A state-space layer updates a fixed-size hidden state with a linear recurrence. Mamba makes the step size and the input and output projections depend on the current token, which lets the model hold or discard information by content, and computes the recurrence with a hardware-aware parallel scan. The steps build the recurrent and parallel views of linear attention, the selective scan and its Mamba-2 simplification; the capstone is the full gated Mamba block with its causal convolution.

steps.name: Linear attention: parallel and recurrent forms
steps.note: The closest attention relative: a fixed-size state updated per token.

steps.name: Mamba-2 gated state scan
steps.note: The follow-up's scalar-decay form, which links SSMs back to attention.

builds.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
builds.blurb: Applied virtual-memory paging to the KV cache, nearly eliminating memory waste in LLM serving and enabling the vLLM engine's large throughput gains.
builds.intro: Each sequence's keys and values are stored in fixed-size blocks allocated on demand from a shared pool, with a block table translating logical positions to physical blocks. That removes the over-reservation and fragmentation of contiguous allocation, lets sequences share prefix blocks with copy-on-write, and lets the scheduler batch many more requests. The steps build the block allocator, capacity planning, attention over a paged cache, prefix caching and a continuous-batching scheduler; the capstone runs a paged decode loop that appends, allocates and attends.

steps.name: Continuous batching
steps.note: The scheduling that paging makes practical.

builds.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
builds.blurb: Got most of the stability of trust-region policy optimisation with a simple clipped objective that allows several epochs of minibatch updates per rollout.
builds.intro: PPO alternates between collecting a rollout and optimising a surrogate objective on it for several epochs. Clipping the probability ratio between the new and old policies stops each update from moving the policy too far from the one that collected the data. Advantages come from generalised advantage estimation with a learned value function, trained jointly with an entropy bonus. The steps build discounted returns, GAE, the actor-critic loss and the clipped surrogate; the capstone is the full multi-epoch update.

lesson_links.t: PPO, LLM Reasoning, Importance Ratio, Advantage

builds.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
builds.blurb: Made very deep networks trainable by having each block learn a residual added to an identity shortcut, winning ImageNet 2015 with 152 layers.
builds.intro: A residual block computes $x + F(x)$, so its default behaviour is the identity and gradients have a direct path through every block. When a block changes resolution or width, the shortcut becomes a strided 1×1 projection. The steps build convolution, batch norm, pooling and both block types; the capstone stacks a stem, residual stages, global average pooling and a classifier.

steps.name: He initialisation
steps.note: The initialisation the same authors derived for ReLU networks.

steps.name: Basic block with a projection shortcut
Bottleneck block
steps.note: The 1×1, 3×3, 1×1 block used in ResNet-50 and deeper.

builds.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
builds.blurb: Encoded position by rotating query and key vectors, so attention scores depend only on relative offsets; now the default in most open LLMs.
builds.intro: RoPE splits each query and key into 2-D pairs and rotates pair $i$ by angle $m\theta_i$ at position $m$. The dot product of a rotated query and key then depends on their positions only through $m - n$, giving relative position information with no extra parameters and no change to the attention kernel. The steps build RoPE in both memory layouts, at arbitrary positions, on a subset of dimensions, for ragged decode batches and for multimodal inputs; the capstone computes attention scores with the frequency rescalings used to extend context length.

steps.name: RoPE in both layouts
steps.note: Interleaved pairs versus split halves: same maths, different weights.

builds.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
builds.blurb: Showed that a deep LSTM encoder and decoder can translate end to end, with source reversal and beam search as key tricks.
builds.intro: One LSTM reads the source (reversed) into a fixed-size state; a second LSTM, initialised with that state, generates the translation one token at a time, and beam search picks the output. The steps build the LSTM cell, batching and teacher-forced training, and beam search; the capstone translates with the full pipeline.

builds.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
builds.blurb: Sped up sampling from large language models two to three times, with an identical output distribution, by verifying a small model's guesses in parallel.
builds.intro: Decoding is memory-bound, so scoring several positions costs the large model about as much as scoring one. A small draft model proposes a few tokens, the target model scores them all in one pass, and a modified rejection-sampling rule accepts a prefix and corrects the first mismatch so the output follows the target distribution exactly. The steps build ordinary sampling, the acceptance test and residual resampling in numpy and JAX; the capstone runs the complete draft-verify loop with two bigram models.

steps.name: Accept, reject and resample in JAX

lesson_links.t: Draft Models, Target Models & Parallel Verification

builds.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
builds.blurb: Simplified mixture-of-experts to top-1 routing with fixed expert capacity and a load-balancing loss, scaling parameter count far beyond compute.
builds.intro: Each token's feed-forward computation goes to one of many experts chosen by a learned router, so parameters grow with the number of experts while FLOPs per token stay fixed. Static shapes force a capacity per expert, which means some tokens can be dropped, and an auxiliary loss keeps the router from collapsing onto a few experts. The steps build routing with load statistics, dispatch and combine, and the communication pattern of expert parallelism; the capstone is a full Switch layer.

steps.name: Capacity-limited routing with balance and z-losses
steps.note: The router z-loss comes from the follow-up ST-MoE paper.

builds.title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
builds.blurb: A two-layer network applied recursively to a latent scratchpad and an answer, trained with deep supervision, beats much larger models on Sudoku, mazes and ARC-AGI puzzles.
builds.intro: TRM simplifies the earlier Hierarchical Reasoning Model to one tiny network and three nested loops: latent recursion (update the scratchpad $z$ several times, then the answer $y$), deep recursion (repeat that, backpropagating only through the last pass), and deep supervision (repeat the whole thing with a loss each time and a learned halting signal). The steps review the small pieces it reuses; the capstone runs the full supervision loop.

steps.name: RMSNorm and a gated MLP
steps.note: The block TRM's tiny network is made of.

steps.name: Binary cross-entropy for the halting head

builds.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
builds.blurb: An encoder-decoder with skip connections at every resolution that produces precise per-pixel segmentations from very few training images.
builds.intro: U-Net contracts the image with convolutions and pooling, expands it again with up-convolutions, and at each level concatenates the encoder's feature map into the decoder so fine detail survives. The original uses unpadded convolutions (hence cropping) and a weighted loss that separates touching cells. The steps build each operation and a one-level U-Net; the capstone is the original valid-convolution design with its weighted loss.

builds.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
builds.blurb: Trained a latent-variable generative model with ordinary backpropagation by maximising a lower bound on the likelihood and rewriting the sampling step so gradients pass through it.
builds.intro: An encoder maps each input to a Gaussian over latents, a decoder maps a latent back to a distribution over inputs, and the loss is the negative evidence lower bound: reconstruction error plus the KL divergence from the encoder's Gaussian to the prior. Sampling $z = \mu + \sigma\epsilon$ with fixed noise $\epsilon$ makes the whole thing differentiable. The steps build the autoencoder, the reparameterised sample, the closed-form KL and the reconstruction loss; the capstone runs one full training step with gradients derived by hand.

steps.name: Plain autoencoder
steps.note: The deterministic version the VAE adds noise and a prior to.

steps.name: KL divergence to a standard normal

builds.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
builds.blurb: Showed that depth built from nothing but stacked 3×3 convolutions and 2×2 pooling steadily improves image classification.
builds.intro: VGG networks are described by a single configuration list of convolution widths and pooling layers, followed by three fully connected layers. The steps cover the 3×3 convolution, the VGG block, pooling, initialisation and dropout in the classifier; the capstone builds any VGG variant from its list and counts its parameters.

steps.name: VGG block: stacked 3×3 convs, then pool

builds.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
builds.blurb: Classifies images with an almost unmodified Transformer encoder by treating fixed-size image patches as tokens.
builds.intro: ViT's only image-specific component is the patch embedding: cut the image into $P \times P$ patches, flatten each, and project it to the model width. A learned `[CLS]` token and a learned position table are added, a pre-LN encoder runs over the sequence, and a linear head reads `[CLS]`. The steps build the input side and the attention sublayer; the capstone runs the full model from pixels to logits.

steps.name: Patch embedding with a class token
2-D position embeddings (alternative)
steps.note: The paper found 1-D learned positions work as well; this is the fixed 2-D variant later models use.

builds.title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
builds.blurb: Learns word vectors by predicting context words, made fast with negative sampling and subsampling of frequent words.
builds.intro: The skip-gram model learns one input vector and one output vector per word so that a word's input vector predicts the output vectors of its neighbours. A full softmax over the vocabulary is too slow, so the paper replaces it with negative sampling: a logistic loss that separates the true context from a few words drawn from a flattened unigram distribution. The steps build the vocabulary, the training data, the loss and the evaluation; the capstone runs a full SGD epoch.

steps.name: Subsampling, dynamic windows and the noise distribution

steps.note: The gradient of the SGNS loss for a single pair.

builds.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
builds.blurb: Framed detection as one regression from the image to a grid of boxes and class probabilities, running in real time with a single network pass.
builds.intro: YOLO divides the image into a grid; each cell predicts a few boxes with confidences and one class distribution, and everything is trained with a weighted sum-squared loss. At test time, class-specific scores are thresholded and duplicates removed with non-maximum suppression. The steps build IoU, box encodings, NMS and a modern box-regression loss; the capstone is the YOLO v1 training loss.

steps.name: Generalised IoU loss
steps.note: What later YOLO versions use instead of squared error on coordinates.
